description: Bis-histidine ligated c-type heme parameters with two covalent thioether bonds to cysteine ligands. Heme residue absorbs the redox-active atoms from 4 protein residues (2 thioether-linked Cys side chains + 2 axial His side chains) following the conste convention; the source Cys and His residues are reduced to backbone-only stubs (CYO and HIO).
references: Henriques, J.; Costa, P. J.; Calhorda, M. J.; Machuqueiro, M. Charge parametrization of the DvH-c3 heme group: Validation using constant (pH,E) molecular dynamics simulations. J. Phys. Chem. B 2013, 117 (1), 70-82. (Source of the bis-His c-heme RESP charges in conste.lib for both oxidized and reduced states.)

Crespo, A.; Martí, M. A.; Kalko, S. G.; Morreale, A.; Orozco, M.; Gelpi, J. L.; Luque, F. J.; Estrin, D. A. Theoretical study of the truncated hemoglobin HbN: Exploring the molecular basis of the NO detoxification mechanism. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127 (12), 4433-4444. (Earlier bis-His heme parameterization; underlies the atom-type scheme and macrocycle bonded parameters in frcmod.conste.)

Guberman-Pfeffer, M. J. Force field parameters for bis-histidine ligated c-type hemes developed using Metal Center Parameter Builder with B3LYP/mixed basis set. Independent re-parameterization for state-distinct Fe-shell bonded parameters.

prerequisites.leaprc_groups_notes: Per-set prerequisites apply (see each forcefield set). The _constpH sets need leaprc.constph + leaprc.conste (PRN lives in conste.lib); the _FixedpH sets are self-contained (PRP/PRD bundled, parm10 types) and need only ff14SB/ff19SB.

Henriques_HCR_RESP_constpH.description: Henriques c-type heme parameters from conste.lib + frcmod.conste, packaged for ProPrep with state-specific oxidized/reduced charge tables. Per-atom charges differ between HCO (Fe³⁺) and HCR (Fe²⁺); bonded terms are state-independent (Henriques did not fork bonded params between redox states).

leaprc_groups.description: Constant-pH titratable protein residues (AS4/GL4 etc.) come from AMBER's constant-pH library.
The titratable PRN heme propionate is defined in AMBER's constant-redox library (conste.lib) - NOT in constph.lib. Constant-(pH,E) MD loads both together (the 'Constant pH + Redox' picker option).

Henriques_HCR_RESP_constpH.name: Henriques bis-His c-heme (conste)
Henriques_HCR_RESP_constpH.methodology:
This is the bis-histidine-ligated c-type heme of cytochrome c, in its reduced (ferrous, Fe2+), low-spin state. It re-packages the published Henriques (2013) 'conste' constant-(pH,redox) parameters for use in ProPrep.

A force field describes the molecule's energy with a few simple terms; here is where each came from:

- Atomic charges (the partial electric charge on each atom, which sets the electrostatic forces): a multi-conformation RESP fit. RESP tunes the charges to reproduce the molecule's quantum-mechanical (QM) electrostatic field; 'multi-conformation' means it was averaged over the four crystallographically distinct hemes of the reference structure (PDB 2CTH, Desulfovibrio vulgaris cytochrome c3) for robustness. The QM was the B3LYP density-functional method with a LANL2TZ(f) basis on iron and 6-31G(d) on the other atoms, on a geometry optimized with the cysteine/histidine attachment carbons restrained to keep the protein-induced heme ruffling. The two redox states share identical bond/angle/torsion terms - the oxidized-vs-reduced difference is carried entirely by the charges (Fe carries +0.666 when ferric and +0.480 when ferrous, with the one-electron difference spread across the macrocycle and ligands).
- Bond, angle, torsion and planarity terms: inherited from the earlier Crespo (2005) bis-His heme model that underlies conste (a classical model fit against QM).
- Custom atom types: the porphyrin nitrogens use conste's NP/NO types; their element and hybridization are registered up front so their implicit-solvent (Born) radii are assigned as nitrogen rather than mis-guessed.
- The heme's two propionate side chains are split off as separate titratable PRN residues; the few extra angle/improper terms they need are folded into this file, so no constant-pH force field need be loaded separately.

Note: building a heme site produces a handful of harmless 'No sp2 improper torsion term' messages - the Crespo/Henriques model keeps the porphyrin and imidazole flat with stiff bond/angle terms instead of out-of-plane improper terms, so tleap notes the missing impropers but the topology is correct.

References: Henriques 2013 (conste charges, multi-conformer RESP); Crespo 2005 (bis-His heme bonded model); Bayly-Cieplak-Cornell-Kollman 1993 (two-stage RESP).

Henriques_HCR_RESP_FixedpH.name: Henriques bis-His c-heme (conste)
Henriques_HCR_RESP_FixedpH.methodology:
FIXED-pH propionate treatment. Identical heme/ligand charges, bonded terms, and atom types as the companion constant-pH set - the ONLY difference is that the two heme propionates are represented by static residues bundled in the lib: PRD (deprotonated carboxylate, COO-, net -1) and PRP (protonated carboxylic acid, COOH, net 0, syn). Each ring's protonation is chosen independently at build time. Loads cleanly under ff14SB/ff19SB with NO leaprc.constph or leaprc.conste dependency. Propionate charges/atoms are taken verbatim from parmed's titratable_residues PRN (state 0 -> PRD, state 1 -> PRP), with the inactive zero-charge ghost hydrogens dropped exactly. Use this set for fixed-protonation MD; use the constant-pH companion set for constant-(pH,E) MD on the propionates.

Henriques_HEH_RESP_constE_constpH.name: Henriques bis-His c-heme (conste)
Henriques_HEH_RESP_constE_constpH.methodology:
CONSTANT-REDOX heme treatment. The heme residue is named HEH, matching AMBER's conste.lib and parmed's titratable_residues.HEH, so ceinutil.py recognises it by name and writes both Fe(III) and Fe(II) charge vectors into the cein/cpein file. Because the oxidation state is chosen at cein-generation time (ceinutil.py -states, or ParmEd) and applied by sander at step 0, ONE library serves both states — exactly as AMBER ships a single HEH unit. The charges in this lib are the oxidized (Fe³⁺, eleccnt=2) set, byte-identical to conste.lib's HEH, and act only as the starting point. Bonded terms are redox-independent in the Henriques/Crespo model, so the frcmod is the same file the fixed-redox sets use.

low_spin.notes_constant_E: The constant_E sets are registered under the oxidized branch only. Under constant_E the topology carries no committed oxidation state — AMBER's single HEH unit ships the ferric charges and ceinutil/sander set the actual state — so a reduced duplicate would be the same file under a second path, which would emit a second loadoff of the same HEH unit. The transformer suppresses the redox_state prompt for constant_E and stamps 'oxidized' so this branch is the one that resolves.

transforms_from: Standard heme residues (HEM, HEC) in the input PDB
2 thioether-linked CYS residues (one each on pyrrole-B and pyrrole-D vinyl-α carbons; identified by closest CYS SG to CAB and CAC respectively)
2 axial HIS residues (proximal + distal; identified by Fe-NE2 coordination bonds)
creates_bonds: Coordination bonds between Fe and 2 axial His NE2 nitrogens (atoms NE21, NE22 inside the heme residue after migration)
Thioether bonds between heme vinyl-α carbons (CAB, CAC) and Cys-SG atoms (atoms SGB2, SGC1 inside the heme residue after migration)
transformation_info.notes: Cys and His side chains are migrated INTO the heme residue (conste convention). After transformation, every redox-active atom lives in HCO/HCR; the source Cys and His residues are left as backbone-only CYO and HIO stubs (just N/H/CA/HA/C/O). The propionates are extracted as PRN residues via the standard pattern (residue ID = heme_id + 1 for propionate A, heme_id + 2 for propionate D).
